Source: Company reports, UBS estimates  
| Summary AMD reported solid numbers and guided about in-line w/ our model -
and better than feared post INTC's guide down - as server CPU upside is more
than offsetting client downside. On top of this, AMD walked up C2027 guidance
to a range that is roughly consistent with our model but well north of Street
numbers as it is (we think) in a better place supply-wise than INTC, both in
terms of wafers and multi-sourced substrate supply. On top of a superior
roadmap, this supply advantage is proving out with this guidance and should
not be under-estimated going forward as both client and server are on N2 (as
opposed to INTC's different nodes) and recent substrate investments are
finally starting to pay off. Gross margin commentary for 2027 - while
consistent with prior 55-56% messaging - is nonetheless encouraging since
commentary suggests ~60% of incremental data center dollars are coming from
the lower-margin GPU business. Net, we walk numbers up once again to ~$19 in
C2027E and ~$30 for C2028E - a range that we long suggested was possible.
C2029 is still a long way out, but once the calendar turns to C2027, this
should become a bigger part of the debate and even assuming a significant
deceleration in growth, we think ~$40 EPS is on the table. While we are
raising numbers, in recognition of multiples having compressed across the
semis landscape, we are bringing our PT down from $730 to $700, but we
maintain Buy. Analysis/Key Highlights

  * Results: AMD reported Sep Q revenue of $13.4B, largely in-line with the top of guidance range and 2% ahead of UBSe/Street. By segment, Data Center was 2% ahead of UBSe; Client 2% behind, and Gaming and Embedded 5% ahead. GM was in-line with our expectations and OpEx ~$75MM lighter, leading to EPS of $2.09, ahead of UBSe $2.00 and $0.14 above Street $1.95.
  * Guidance: FQ4 (Dec) revenue was guided to $17B (midpt) - or essentially in-line w/ our model, but above Street ~$16.3B and better than feared following INTC's guide down. AMD's client guidance is a little better than INTC but in the same general range, as upside to server CPU is providing a very strong offset since AMD is in a very strong supply position with a vastly superior roadmap, in our view. Gross margin was guided to 55% - down ~100bps Q/Q but consistent with messaging from management over the past few Qs given the big ramp in data center GPU (which, based on mgmt commentary, seems to be in the ~$7B range, or up a little less than 2x Q/Q). 
  * Forward commentary: Coming into the call, the big debate was whether management would walk up C2027 data center revenue so soon after having provided its initial guidance last Q. As part of total C2027 revenue that AMD now sees up >80%, management walked up server CPU revenue guidance from >70% to >100%, with data center GPU up "significantly more" than this. Additionally, it expects data center to be >80% of total revenue next year. Commentary on PC was largely similar to INTC, and AMD expects to again outgrow the TAM in C2027, but CQ1 will be down another 10%+ after CQ4 being down >20% Q/Q - again roughly in the same ballpark as INTC. The major difference here is that AMD does not expect the slowdown in server CPU revenue that INTC signaled for CQ1 - we think in part due to much more supply fungibility for AMD as everything is on N2 and it has a more diversified substrate supply situation as well. 
  * Gross margin:Despite DC GPU becoming a much larger part of the mix and carrying below-corporate-average GM, management seems comfortable with CQ4 as a reasonable benchmark for 2027. Specifically, the company seems okay with GM remaining in the ~55-56% range next year, which makes sense to us given DC GPU should contribute substantially more incremental revenue dollars next year than server CPU (~$30B versus ~$20B). Some ability to pass through higher HBM/component costs through LT customer agreements should also provide an offset as input costs rise, helping support GM despite the much larger GPU mix.
  * Server CPU: Server CPU remains very strong with both cloud and enterprise growing >2x Y/Y in 3Q, and the growth continues to come mostly from units/core count rather than ASP. Demand is still running above supply and the company is working to secure additional capacity, while Venice appears to be off to a strong start with initial demand tracking better than prior EPYC launches. We estimate server CPU to be ~$17B in C2026 and could very well get close to $40B in C2027, as AMD continues to take share across cloud/enterprise while also benefiting from incremental CPU demand around AI head nodes.
  * DC GPU: DC GPU was a little over $3.5B in 3Q and should step up significantly from here as MI455X/Helios ramp across META, MSFT, OAI, and ORCL. Visibility into 2027 continues to improve, with deployments mapped to specific data centers and AMD working with customers well in advance on power, infrastructure and supply requirements. We think low-$40Bs of DC GPU revenue in C2027 is achievable given the stronger demand outlook and additional supply secured since last quarter, which would make DC GPU larger than server CPU for the full year.
  * Client: Sell-through weakened late in 3Q and AMD is now managing sell-in more closely with end demand as the channel works through inventory. We think the correction likely extends into 1H27, with higher memory/component costs putting additional pressure on a PC market that management expects to be down -DD% next year. That said, AMD should continue to outperform the market through share gains in premium DT and enterprise NB, while the fungibility of supply between client/server gives the company flexibility to shift capacity toward the much stronger server market.
  * Embedded: The segment continued to recover in 3Q and has now seen four straight Qs of accelerating growth. Management expects growth to strengthen further in 2027 as the design win pipeline ramps, although CQ1 should still be seasonally down. We continue to think Embedded becomes a more meaningful contributor as we move through next year and, given the higher GM profile of the business, should provide some offset to the negative mix impact from the much faster growth in DC GPU.

Read Across

* While we see limited read through here for INTC, the server growth is generally positive for ARM, but AMD did highlight its recent gains for head-node applications attached to XPU racks for customers like OpenAI. The read through on GPU and NVDA tells us what we already know - that demand is very strong and customers like META and OpenAI (who have warrant deals with AMD) are taking product as expected, in part because they are nominally getting ~$13B in value per GW of product they take - ergo, the warrants nearly pay for the deal for these customers. 
Valuation: PT $700 (from $730) We lower our price target from $730 to $700,
derived from a 23x multiple (27x previously) applied to C28E EPS of $29.83
(from $26.94).

# Advanced Micro Devices

## Strong Results and Guide; Total Revenues Set to Grow 80%+ in CY27 With Data
Center More Than Doubling and Embedded Continuing Its Cyclical Recovery;
Raising Out-Year Estimates

  
---  
  
By Harlan Sur
AC,
Apoorva
Kumar

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Neutral  
---  
AMD, AMD US  
Price (03 Nov 26):$483.90  
**▲** Price Target (Dec-27):$575.00  
Prior (Dec-27):$550.00  
  
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) delivered a strong set of 3Q26 results, with an
even stronger out-quarter guide that came in ahead of both consensus
expectations and the buyside estimates we heard coming into the print. The
team went one step further and provided a strong 80%+ total revenue growth
outlook for CY27 (Street was modeling ~75% growth off a lower CY26 number
before the call), driven by >2x growth in its Data Center (DC) business and
continued growth in Embedded. The team is benefitting from continued strong AI
infrastructure spending dynamics, the ramp of its MI455X “Helios” rackscale AI
compute platform, and strong agentic-driven server CPU demand. The team’s
Embedded business (FPGA + embedded CPU) continues to see cyclical recovery and
strong demand trends in A&D / industrial segments. Slightly offsetting these
strong growth dynamics is the well-telegraphed weakness in the PC client
market, with the AMD team noting that it started to observe a slowdown in
sell-through near the end of 3Q as high memory pricing/component costs weighed
on demand. Looking into 2027, AMD expects a DD % decline in overall PC unit
TAM, however, this is being more than offset by the >2x growth in DC (which
will represent >80% of total revenues in CY27). The team has done a good job
of continuing to secure more supply (wafers, advanced packaging, components)
to support the solid growth in CY27 and with demand still outstripping supply,
we believe further capacity becoming available over the next two quarters
could support continued upward revisions to revenue and EPS estimates through
2027. Separately, we estimate that AMD gained server CPU share in 3Q and
expect further gains in 4Q and through CY27. All told, we remain impressed
with the company’s execution and are raising our CY26/CY27 estimates and PT to
$575 (up from $550 prior) on the back of Tuesday’s results.

  * Strong Q3 results, driven by the ramp of MI455X (AI GPU) “Helios” platform, continued strong demand in server CPUs, and cyclical recovery in embedded; PC client weakness starting to unfold... AMD reported 3Q26 revenues of $13.4B (+45% Y/Y, +16% Q/Q), coming in ahead of Street consensus of ~$13.1B. Data Center revenue of $8.55B (+97% Y/Y, +27% Q/Q) drove the beat, with server CPU up >90% Y/Y (cloud/enterprise segments up 2x Y/Y) and up ~20% Q/Q. DC GPU revenue grew strongly Q/Q (we estimate +35% Q/Q) as the team commenced the ramp of its MI455X rackscale compute platform. Client declined 4% Q/Q as AMD saw PC market sell-through weakness materialize towards the end of the quarter, while Gaming continued to further decline ~1% Q/Q. Embedded was up 14% Q/Q (+29% Y/Y), driven by broad-based demand across networking, A&D, test & measurement, and communications customers, with embedded x86 emerging as a significant growth driver as hyperscalers and networking customers increasingly adopt AMD CPUs for control-plane functions in the DC. GMs of 56% remained flat Q/Q and in-line with expectations, whereas EPS of $2.09 came in better than expected (Street at $1.97) on higher revenues and lower opex. 

  * Strong Q4 guide and impressive 2027 growth outlook, with management expecting 80%+ growth in CY27... AMD guided 4Q26 revenues to ~$17.0B ± 3%, with the midpoint standing above Street estimates ($16.3B) and the buyside expectations we had heard coming into results. The Q4 guide implies ~27% Q/Q growth, driven by an expected ~50% sequential increase in DC revenue as AI accelerator shipments ramp and as EPYC adoption continues. Embedded revenues are also expected to grow DD Q/Q in Q4, though note that there is a partial offset due to >20% sequential declines in Client and Gaming. On the margin front, AMD guided non-GAAP GMs to ~55% (vs. Street estimates at ~55.5%). Looking further out, management highlighted its expectations for 80%+ total company growth in CY27 (more than 2x the LT growth estimates AMD laid out at its Nov-25 Investor Day), with Data Center accounting for >80% of sales. Server CPU revenue is expected to double Y/Y, while Data Center AI revenue is expected to grow significantly faster, supported by the MI450/Helios ramp and continued EPYC share gains. Although the growing AI mix may pressure corporate GMs, management expects opex to grow at less than half the rate of revenue, supporting meaningful operating leverage through 2027.

  * Increasing forward estimates and raising PT to $575 (up from $550 prior)... On the back of tonight’s strong results and outlook, we are increasing our out-year estimates and raising our PT to $575. Our PT is based on ~22x our CY28 EPS of $26.50, with the multiple standing in-line with the broader semiconductor group average (~20-25x).

# Arista

## 3Q26 Review: Scaling Out, Across, and (Soon) Up as the Initial 2027 Guide
Clears the Bar; Reit. OW

  
---  
  
By Joseph Cardoso
AC,
Marc
Vitenzon,
Manmohanpreet
Singh

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
ANET, ANET US  
Price (03 Nov 26):$169.91  
**▲** Price Target (Dec-27):$270.00  
Prior (Dec-27):$250.00  
  
Arista pushed back on worries heading into the earnings print about data
center investment longevity and whether its first-look at 2027 would be
conservative as management guided 2027 revenue growth of +38%-40%, or above
the high end of investor expectations for the guide of +35%, which was on top
of a raised 2026 outlook of +48%. The 2027 outlook rests on themes we have
been highlighting, including a still-expanding scale-out market, with a fast-
growing scale-across business layering on top (30% of AI revenue in 2026; mix
likely to expand in 2027), and to be shortly joined by a scale-up business,
with trials starting in 2027, production in 2028; although conservative
revenue recognition (deferred) could mask projects going live in 2027 itself.
The aforementioned supports Arista to guide for a doubling in AI fabrics
revenue to $7 bn in 2027, which is before considering Campus revenue expected
to expand +60% to $2 bn, led by security-driven refreshes (Mythos/Glasswing),
and the rest implied to expand +11% to $9.5 bn, the latter of which we expect
has room for upside. Gross margin also came in better than expected, as
management set its first look at 62%-64% for 2027, despite memory and silicon
inflation, supported by supply chain efficiencies and multi-year supply
agreements, price increases, and customer mix spreading past the largest Cloud
Titans. The one nitpick was deferred revenue, which dipped sequentially,
although management argued the move reflects healthy turnover rather than
fading demand, as more deferred revenue was released this quarter than last
and was offset by larger new additions, and reiterated that deferred revenue
should end 2026 above 2025 levels. Stepping back, Arista is turning its
technical lead in scale-out and scale-across, along with its emerging position
in scale-up, into a steadily broader customer base, which now spans more than
100 Etherlink AI customers, more than 10 GW of deployments across 10 or more
accelerator types expected by end-2027, and three to four 10%+ customers
expected in 2026 (vs. two in 2025), all within a market now sized at $220 bn+
by 2030 (vs. $105 bn a year ago, which did not include scale-up), giving the
company more room to sustain a higher growth rate in our view. To that end, we
are raising our revenue and earnings estimates, lifting our Dec-27 price
target to $270 (vs. $250 prior), and reiterating our OW rating.

  * 3Q26 (Sep-end) Results: EPS beat driven by stronger revenue and gross margin, partly offset by higher opex. Revenue increased +58.5% y/y to $3,658 mn (vs. JPMe of $3,300 mn, consensus of $3,334 mn, and prior guide of $3,300 mn), led by a +67% y/y increase in Product revenue to $3,190 mn and a +18% y/y increase in Services revenue to $468 mn, with growth led by AI and Enterprise customers. Gross margin tracked to 64.0% (vs. JPMe of 62.9%, consensus of 63.0%, and prior guide of ~63%) up 60 bps q/q on customer mix, but down 120 bps y/y (65.2%) as supply chain efficiencies only partly offset product cost inflation. Operating margin tracked to 49.1% (vs. JPMe of 48.4%, consensus of 48.8%, and guide of 48-49%), reflecting strong operating leverage despite elevated R&D investment in AI and liquid-cooled platforms. Consequently, EPS tracked to $1.20 vs. JPMe of $1.07 and consensus of $1.08.
  * 4Q26 (Dec-end) Guidance: Revenue and EPS guided well above expectations. Revenues were guided to $3,900 mn-$4,000 mn, or $3,950 mn at midpoint (vs. JPMe of $3,605 mn and consensus of $3,573 mn), implying growth of +59% y/y and +8% q/q. Gross margins were guided to 63%-64% (vs. JPMe of 63.0% and consensus of 62.9%), while operating margins were guided to 48-49% (vs. JPMe of 48.0% and consensus of 48.9%). Lastly, EPS was guided to $1.26-$1.30, or $1.28 at midpoint, vs. JPMe of $1.14 and consensus of $1.14. The quarterly revenue midpoint positions 2026 revenue just over $13.3 bn, implying approximately +48% y/y growth.
  * 2027 Guidance: Initial outlook calls for continued strong growth, led by AI fabrics and Campus. Revenue was guided to growth of +38-40% y/y (versus 32.0% y/y JPMe and 30.0% y/y consensus), against the approximately $13.3 bn FY2026 guidance baseline, equating to approximately $18.5 bn at midpoint. AI fabrics revenue is targeted to double to approximately $7 bn from a $3.5 bn 2026 target, while Campus revenue is expected to grow approximately +60% to $2 bn from a $1.25 bn FY2026 target, with management expecting double-digit growth across the remaining businesses. Gross margins were guided to 62-64% (versus 63.0% JPMe and 62.7% consensus) and operating margin to approximately 49% (versus 49.0% JPMe and 48.7% consensus).

# Arista

## 3Q26 Preview: Pullback Creates a Favorable Setup as 2027 Growth
Opportunities Broaden; Reit. OW

  
---  
  
By Joseph Cardoso
AC,
Marc
Vitenzon,
Manmohanpreet
Singh

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
ANET, ANET US  
Price (30 Oct 26):$168.86  
Price Target (Dec-27):$250.00  
  
We are positive on the setup for Arista shares heading into the 3Q26 print
with the stock down -14% since 2Q26 earnings (vs. -14% for AI peers and -2%
for S&P 500), amid concerns about the durability of the AI infrastructure
buildout, Arista’s exposure to hyperscaler and AI Lab customers, and the
possibility of conservative initial 2027 guidance given management’s typical
prudence and ongoing supply tightness. In our view, that caution creates a
favorable setup with intra-quarter revisions to end-market forecasts (see
industry model report
here) and hyperscaler capex outlooks (see cloud capex report
here) remaining supportive, large customer ramps on the horizon,
including Google and AI Lab customers, and scale-across and scale-up
opportunities layering onto a growing scale-out business. Notably, our review
of Arista’s prior 3Q guidance practices suggests the company has increasingly
set its initial full-year revenue outlook near consensus, then delivered
upside as the year progressed. With consensus currently forecasting revenue
growth of +29% y/y in 2027, we see +30% as a reasonable starting point that
investors would likely receive neutrally to positively based on our
discussions, while an outlook of +35% (or greater) would likely be received
more favorably. Importantly, we see a path to that higher starting figure,
even under conservative 2027 scenarios (see below), with sources of upside to
raise the outlook through the year including Arista’s share of hyperscaler
capex, which we forecast to grow close to +70% in 2027, the opportunity
associated with leading AI Lab customer deployments, and stronger growth
across the rest of the business, including DCI/scale-across, enterprise DC and
campus switching, as well as scale-up. We expect Arista’s updated TAM to also
reinforce the aforementioned, as we estimate it reaching $340 bn+ by 2030 vs.
$105 bn for 2029 issued in September 2025, implying a 30%+ CAGR over the
remainder of the decade. That could also set the stage for an upgrade to
Arista’s three-year revenue growth target, which it raised to 20%+ from the
mid-teens in May. Net-net, we are constructive heading into the print as we
expect a 3Q26 beat and a raise, accompanied by favorable 2027 initial
guidance, and the eventual step-up in the long-term growth expectations.
Reiterate Overweight.

  * 3Q26 Results: Revenue, margins and EPS to track ahead of JPMe, consensus, and guidance. JPMe forecasts revenue of $3.30 bn versus consensus of $3.33 bn and management guidance of approximately $3.30 bn. JPMe operating margin of 48.3% compares with consensus of 48.8% and guidance of 48%–49%, while JPMe EPS of $1.07 compares with consensus of $1.08 and guidance of $1.06–$1.08. JPMe gross margin is 62.8% versus consensus of 63.0%. 
  * 4Q26 Outlook: Revenue and earnings outlook to exceed JPMe and consensus expectations. JPMe 2026 revenue is $12.65 bn versus consensus of $12.69 bn. For 4Q, JPMe forecasts revenue of $3.61 bn versus consensus of $3.57 bn, operating margin of 47.9% versus 48.9%, and EPS of $1.14 versus $1.14.
  * Key Watch Points: Key watch points heading into the upcoming earnings print include commentary on the demand environment and risks as they relate to Tier 2/Neoclouds in particular, the magnitude and timing of the scale-up opportunity (including rack versus switch tray margins), as well as supply availability, especially related to the latest generation switching silicon. Furthermore, we would expect a focus on how Arista continues to navigate component cost inflation and the implications to gross margins. 



#

## Larger TAM and Customer Ramps Strengthen Case for Solid Initial 2027 Guide

### Historical guidance patterns point to a ~30% initial 2027 revenue growth
target

In recent years, Arista’s initial guidance for the following year has
typically landed near consensus, which currently calls for revenue growth of
+29% y/y and an operating margin of ~47% in 2027. If that pattern holds, we
expect Arista to begin the year with a revenue growth target of around +30%.

reports, J.P. Morgan estimates.  
---|---  
  
### Larger TAM of $340 bn+ by 2030 (30%+ CAGR) could support a more ambitious
initial 2027 guide

Historically, Arista has broken its TAM outlook into Data Center Ethernet
Switch and Campus Switch, along with a residual bucket containing software and
wireless, among other smaller markets (e.g., security, WAN). Since Arista
presented its $105 bn 2029 TAM in September 2025, which was based on 650
Group’s 1Q25 forecast, 650 Group has revised the 2029 DC Ethernet Switch TAM
by +170% (primarily on account of DC AI Switch) and the Campus Switch TAM by
+17%.

We expect the 2030 TAM presented alongside the 3Q26 earnings print to reflect
both revisions and, for the first time, include scale-up switching, which 650
Group sizes at $102 bn in 2030. We also see upside in the residual category as
Arista’s exposure to DCI expands. The DCI switching and routing market is
expected to expand from $4 bn in 2026 to $22 bn in 2030, implying a +56% CAGR.
Outside DCI, we conservatively assume the residual category grows at a +5%
CAGR over the remainder of the decade.

Taken together, these assumptions imply Arista’s TAM could expand at a 30%+
CAGR to $340 bn+ by 2030, including 40%+ growth in 2027. That larger
opportunity could give management room to set a more ambitious initial revenue
growth outlook ahead of the +30% range.

---|---  
  
### Hyperscalers and AI Lab ramps to conservatively support at least 40%+
revenue growth in 2027

Combining our forecasts for hyperscaler revenue, the AI Lab customer’s TPU
ramp via Broadcom, and a conservative +5% y/y growth assumption for the
remaining business yields 2027 revenue growth of 40%+ y/y for Arista. That
compares with guidance for +40% y/y growth in 2026 and a +27% revenue CAGR
from 2022 to 2025. In our 2027 build, hyperscalers contribute roughly 25
percentage points of growth, the AI lab customer roughly 15 points, and the
remaining customers roughly 3 points. We see the latter assumption as a
readily identifiable source of upside.

With regard to the AI Lab customer, Broadcom has said it expects its AI Lab
customer to deploy 1 GW of TPUs in 2026, followed by another 5 GW in 2027, at
an estimated capex of $20-$30 bn per GW. We believe Arista could participate
in the scale-across network and/or spine layer, which together represent an
estimated ~10% of that spending. Assuming $125 bn of capex for the 5 GW
deployment in 2027 and a conservative share of the addressable opportunity, we
estimate Arista could generate $2 bn+ of revenue from the customer that year.

### Revenue growth of 40%+ assumes continued share loss at Cloud Titans

According to 650 Group, Arista’s share in DC Ethernet Switch for Hyperscalers
has steadily eroded over the last three years, in part due to its limited
exposure to Google and Amazon, with market share peaking at 38% in 2Q23 and
tracking to a new low at 26% in 2Q26, while both Celestica and Cisco have
experienced share gains during the period.

Source: 650 Group

In our forecast, we conservatively assume that Arista's share in the
Hyperscaler DC Ethernet Switch Market (excluding scale-across and scale-up)
continues to trend lower. That said, overall share of Hyperscaler capex may
benefit from expanding opportunities in scale-out as well as in scale-across
and scale-up, particularly amid indications of share expansion at Google via
the Virgo Network, as well as possible upside to the Microsoft relationship
given a recently
announced scale-up engagement.

Nonetheless, even as Arista’s share of the Hyperscaler DC Ethernet Switch
Market declines, we estimate Arista can grow revenue from hyperscalers by 50%+
y/y in 2027. That compares with our forecast for hyperscaler capex growth of
+69% y/y in 2027 (+65% y/y ex-Amazon), following +95% in 2026. Separately, 650
Group estimates the Hyperscaler DC Ethernet Switch TAM will grow +69% y/y in
2027, following +58% in 2026.

Figure 9: Hyperscaler DC Ethernet TAM and Arista’s Share

$ bn, % y/y [RHS]



Source: J.P. Morgan Estimates, 650 Group

The rest of Arista’s business spans DCI/AI scale-across (+88% y/y market
growth in 2027), DC Ethernet Switch Ex-Hyperscaler and Neoclouds (+20% y/y),
and Campus Switching (+5% y/y). Our assumption of +5% y/y growth for this
business is therefore conservative as it matches the slowest growing of those
markets, even though much of Arista’s exposure is to faster growing data
center opportunities, likely representing low-hanging upside to our outlook.

# Investment Thesis, Valuation and Risks

### Arista (Overweight; Price Target: $250.00)

### Investment Thesis

We rate Arista Overweight and expect further upside in revenue and earnings
estimates, led by 1) the continuation of the ramp in Arista’s AI revenues; 2)
a robust upgrade cycle for networking equipment with cloud customers; 3)
revenue upside from better-than-expected performance in Enterprise; 4) higher-
than-peer-group growth outlook in the long term.

### Valuation

We are maintaining our December 2027 price target of $250, based on valuing
our 2028E EPS estimate at a 45x P/E multiple. We believe our target P/E
multiple is appropriate as it represents a premium to the 2-year multiple
average of ~40x and a substantial premium to the long-term average of ~30x,
justified by visibility into accelerating growth driven by both the AI data
center build-out as well as Arista’s Enterprise opportunity.

ANET P/E-Based Price Target Analysis

$ mn, except per share data



Source: J.P. Morgan estimates.

### Risks to Rating and Price Target

#### Industry Downside Risks

Adoption of white box solutions remains a threat. While it is difficult to
drive superior performance using white box solutions (non-branded switches
available off the shelf) relative to switches from established technology
leaders like Arista or Cisco, the improving capabilities of the white box
solutions over time could drive customers to use them for parts of the network
with lower performance requirements. Faster-than-expected adoption of white
box solutions could imply downside to our Arista earnings forecasts and price
target.

#### Company-Specific Downside Risks

Faster-than-expected shift toward disaggregated software solutions from data
center customers could challenge Arista. Arista delivers industry-leading
switching technology through a combination of hardware and software, although
a significant portion of the value-add is driven by software. While Arista has
already started to offer disaggregated software products to its customers,
these do not yet account for a significant portion of revenues. A faster-than-
expected shift from customers toward proprietary software and generic hardware
could create competitive challenges for Arista.

## Solid 3Q Execution, But Choppy N-T Trends & Lower Estimates 2027-2028

BKNG executed well in 3Q, coming in above guidance across all key metrics,
including Room Nights (345M, +7% growth), Gross Bookings ($54.5B, +10%
reported & +11% FXN), Adjusted Revenue ($9.8B, +9% reported & +10% FXN), &
Adjusted EBITDA ($4.6B, +9% & 47% margin, flat Y/Y). Room nights accelerated
in 3Q as int'l travel improved in Europe & Asia, including slight expansion in
the booking window in Europe & globally. US room night growth remained stable
at a HSD level. BKNG also continued to navigate Middle East air impacts
including elevated airfares & reduced capacity. However, the 4Q backdrop is
choppier as BKNG saw global demand moderation toward the end of 3Q, ongoing
air pressures tied to the Middle East, some impact from civil unrest in
Europe, & US growth trending lower given macro concerns & tougher comps. As a
result, BKNG's 4Q outlook came in below expectations, including 1-3% RN growth
& 4-6% FXN GB growth. For ABNB & EXPE, we believe their heavier US mix leaves
them more insulated from the international & long-haul headwinds weighing on
BKNG, and resilient US domestic trends likely bode well for both. In terms of
AI product & progress, BKNG saw customer service costs decline in 3Q even
w/higher booking volumes. And even though AI tools are not broadly rolled out,
Booking.com daily AI search visitors were up 10x Q/Q in 3Q, & platforms like
Vayo, Priceline's Penny, Agoda, & OpenTable are seeing a mix of higher
engagement, conversion rates, booking value, & incrementality. Importantly,
BKNG continues to build its own AI & agentic tools directly into its products,
while also partnering w/agents & LLMs, even though the latter account for well
under 1% of RNs. We're encouraged by BKNG's execution, along w/the early
outlook for healthy growth in 1H27 based on already booked business. However,
4Q trends are choppier & our 2027-2028 estimates are moving lower. We maintain
our Overweight rating, but lower our PT from $248 to $205 on ~15.5x our ‘28E
GAAP EPS of $13.33.

  * Solid 3Q, But 4Q Weighed By Mixed Backdrop. Stronger Int’l travel from Europe & Asia bookers drove the RN acceleration in 3Q, while domestic held steady at +HSD%. By booker region, EU & Asia grew +HSD% and the US & RoW grew +MSD%. FXN ADRs rose ~3%, led by Europe. However, demand moderated late in the quarter, and October was hit by ME disruptions, elevated airfares, & unrest in certain European cities. The 4Q guide assumes these impacts persist through year-end and includes a ~200 bps FX headwind. GBs is expected to grow +4-6% FXN & Revs +2-4% FXN in 4Q. Adj. EBITDA is expected to stay ~flat, w/higher planned investments in verticals, AI, & tech weighing in 4Q. Importantly, mgmt said 1H27 on-the-books trends look healthy. While this is early and subject to cancellations, we believe it points to N-T disruption rather than a broader slowdown & mgmt. remains committed its ambition to grow top-line 8%+ FXN.
  * Early AI Benefits. Mgmt flagged early gains in four areas: 1) engagement, with Booking.com daily AI search visitors up 10x Q/Q; 2) conversion, with Penny & Agoda AI assistant users converting at ~2x the rate of non-users; 3) booking value, ~20% higher for Agoda AI assistant users; and 4) incrementality, with OpenTable seating 190K covers via OpenAI in September. LLM referrals have picked up in recent weeks but remain well below 1% of Booking.com RNs. BKNG is also testing its AI-native platforms Lola & Vayo, and Agoda is connected directly to META’s Muse in Asia. On costs, customer service costs fell despite higher volumes. Agoda’s cost per 1M tokens fell 25%+ between June & September. Importantly, mgmt noted horizontal agents prefer to partner with aggregators rather than connect directly to suppliers.
  * Other Notable Points. 1) The ~$900M revenue reduction & ~$100M accrued loss relate to the FTC case on Priceline Partner Solutions. The charge is excluded from adjusted results, and we view it as largely non-recurring. 2) Connected Trip transactions grew ~20% to a LDD% share of Booking.com transactions, while flights grew +19% and attractions +24%, both accelerating Q/Q. 3) BKNG on track to combine its B2B units on Jan 1. B2B affiliate commissions drove +11% marketing growth, while B2C delivered leverage. 4) BKNG remains on track for $650M of transformation run-rate savings in 2027. 5) Merchant mix rose ~300 bps to ~75% of GBs, and Genius L2 & L3 and the mobile app each now drive a high-50s% share of RNs.

# Hardware & Networking

## F1Q27 Optical Preview: Strong Demand and Improving Capacity Support Upside;
However, Valuation Favors COHR and FN Over LITE

  
---  
  
By Joseph Cardoso
AC,
Manmohanpreet
Singh,
Marc
Vitenzon

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

Heading into F1Q27 (Sep-end) earnings, we expect optical fundamentals to
remain solid with most of our intra-quarter checks pointing to strong demand
through year-end and into CY27, while LTAs extend visibility into CY28 and
beyond. Growth in TRx and associated components, including lasers, is now
being joined by more material ramps in higher margin DCI, OCS, and CPO/NPO
opportunities, which we expect to contribute increasingly to revenue and
profitability in coming quarters. Delivering to upsides though will depend in
part on capacity expansions, including InP lasers, and making progress on
those ramps will be a crucial watch point for estimates. We expect management
teams to emphasize both the strength of underlying demand and their progress
on capacity; however, investors are likely to focus on the nuanced details,
including: (1) the pace of the 1.6T TRx ramp, particularly given laser and DSP
constraints, and its pricing and margin benefits; (2) OCS upside with Google
and opportunities with other customers; (3) confidence in CPO timing/sizing
amid continued noise on supply chain challenges; and (4) NPO timing and
architecture choices, including implications for content (ELS vs. ILS, UHP vs.
MP lasers vs. VCSEL). Even these questions, and the earnings themselves, may
be partly overshadowed by the recent focus on consolidation between
optoelectronic and semiconductor assets, including the strategic rationale,
potentially underappreciated synergies, and the likelihood of a transaction
given recent valuations and regulatory hurdles.

To that end, while we remain broadly bullish on optical fundamentals over both
the near- and long-term, the setup into the upcoming prints varies by company.
Given those differences, we believe investors may need to be more selective:

  * Most favorable on Coherent. Shares trade at 12x CY28 earnings, the largest discount within the group, and we see scope for upward revenue and earnings revisions, though margin upside may be more moderate as lower margin TRx revenue continues to drive the near-term upside. That said, the valuation suggests investor expectations remain muted with the margin dynamics likely already well understood. 
  * Fabrinet follows. Shares trade at 14x CY28 earnings, and we expect concerns around Datacom and HPC to ease as improving Nvidia-TRx and AWS-HPC ramps drive revenue and earnings upside, while continued DCI momentum and a more material AWS-TRx ramp add to that strength. The reaction may be tempered, however, by the limited visibility provided by the new segmentation and how much detail management provides on Nvidia-TRx and AWS-HPC, which have drawn greater investor attention in recent quarters. 
  * Somewhat more cautious on Lumentum. Investors appear to be anticipating a significant beat in both results and outlook, while shares trade at a sizable premium to the group at 21x CY28 earnings. That combination could invite closer scrutiny of the quality of the upside, particularly if a material portion comes from lower margin TRx revenue and results in more subdued margin performance than in recent quarters.



## Lumentum (LITE): Expected Beat and Raise Meets a High Bar; TRx Mix Could
Test Margin Performance

We are somewhat cautious on Lumentum’s setup into the print, despite expecting
a beat-and-raise, as shares already trade at 21x CY28 earnings, a sizable
premium to the group, and investors appear to be anticipating meaningful beats
in both results and outlook with buy-side CY28 earnings expectations tracking
well ahead of sell-side consensus. That said, we expect the results to confirm
that near-term CPO/NPO and OCS opportunities remain on track with management’s
prior expectations, while pointing to greater medium- and long-term upside in
both. On the flipside, we expect more immediate upside is likely to come from
Datacom lasers, DCI solutions such as pump lasers, and Datacom TRx, of which
the relative upside driven by the latter could weigh on gross margin
performance, particularly relative to recent quarters, drawing increased
scrutiny at the current valuation. Nonetheless, we are embedding modest upside
from these drivers in our model, with our estimates continuing to track ahead
of consensus. We reiterate our December 2027 price target of $1,280, based on
a ~29x multiple of our updated CY28 EPS estimate, the highest among optical
peers, reflecting Lumentum’s leading growth and margin profile.

  * F1Q27 (Sep-end) Results: Expect EPS beat driven by better than consensus revenue and margins. We are forecasting revenue of $1,273 mn vs. consensus $1,256 mn and guidance of $1,225-$1,275 mn, representing growth of +138% y/y. Meanwhile, we are forecasting gross margins of 51.3% (vs. consensus of 51.3%) and operating margins of 40.3% (vs. consensus of 39.9% and guidance of 39.5%-40.5%), which leads to our earnings forecast of $4.29 (vs. consensus of $4.21 and guidance of $4.05-$4.35).
  * F2Q27 (Dec-end) Guidance: Revenue and earnings outlook expected to track ahead of consensus expectations. We are forecasting revenue of $1,531 mn vs. consensus $1,485 mn, representing growth of +130% y/y. Meanwhile, we are forecasting gross margins of 51.5% (vs. consensus of 51.6%) and operating margins of 41.6% (vs. consensus of 41.0%), which leads to our earnings forecast of $5.28 (vs. consensus of $5.07).



## Coherent (COHR): Low Valuation Offers a Favorable Setup; Path to
Accelerating Margin Improvement Remains in Focus

We see a positive setup for Coherent heading into its F1Q27 earnings print,
with revenue and earnings upside supported by continued progress on the InP
capacity ramp. Specifically, we expect data center revenue growth to
accelerate to more than 80%+ y/y, exceeding our +80% forecast, as additional
InP capacity unlocks TRx revenue. Given much of that upside is likely to come
from lower margin TRx, we expect gross margin upside to remain more limited,
despite the benefits from conitnued strong demand for higher margin
DCI/Telecom opportunities. In our view, that mix dynamic is already reflected
in muted investor expectations, with shares trading at 12x CY28 earnings, the
largest discount in the group. Beyond the quarter, we expect investors to
focus on the breadth and timing of newer, higher margin revenue streams,
including OCS, multi-rail, and CPO/NPO and how quickly those ramps can
accelerate gross margin improvement even as lower margin TRx demand continues
to grow. Investors will also look for commentary on the ramp of higher priced
and margin 1.6T TRx and its potential to ease the margin pressure associated
with the product set. Taken together, we expect a near-term beat-and-raise led
primarily by TRx upside, as well as a contribution from DCI/Telecom, against a
backdrop of undemanding valuation and muted sentiment. That said, we are
lowering our Dec-27 price target to $385 (vs. $465 prior) based on a lower
target multiple, consistent with the current NTM trading multiple and below
the multiple we ascribe to Lumentum, given Coherent’s lower growth and margin
profile.

  * F1Q27 (Sep-end) Results: Revenue and earnings to track ahead of consensus expectations into the print. We are forecasting revenue of $2,390 mn vs. consensus $2,311 mn and guidance of $2,200-$2,400 mn, representing growth of +51% y/y. Meanwhile, we are forecasting gross margins of 40.5% (vs. consensus of 40.6% and guidance of 39.5-41.5%) and operating margins of 22.9% (vs. consensus of 23.0%), which leads to our earnings forecast of $2.08 (vs. consensus of $2.01 and guidance of $1.85-$2.05).
  * F2Q27 (Dec-end) Guidance: Anticipate revenue and earnings outlook to track ahead of sell-side estimates. We are forecasting revenue of $2,567 mn vs. consensus $2,552 mn, representing growth of +52% y/y. Meanwhile, we are forecasting gross margins of 40.8% (vs. consensus of 40.8%) and operating margins of 23.7% (vs. consensus of 23.4%), which leads to our earnings forecast of $2.30 (vs. consensus of $2.24).



## Fabrinet (FN): Multiple Ramps Set Up FY27 Growth for Acceleration; Though
Program Visibility Could Be a Watch Point

We are somewhat positive on Fabrinet heading into its F1Q27 earnings print, as
it should offer a proof point that multiple product ramps are supporting an
acceleration in FY27 revenue growth relative to FY26, against a backdrop of
shares trading at 14x CY28 earnings. Among the opportunities in focus for
investors, we believe management remains confident in improving Nvidia TRx
revenue in F1Q27 and beyond, particularly now that transceivers are shipping
with EMLs from multiple suppliers. We see a similar setup for AWS HPC with the
transition to the next-generation solution now largely complete, opening a
much larger opportunity than the prior generation and potential for Fabrinet
to gain share. AWS TRx and merchant TRx programs should add to those ramps in
the near term, with AWS TRx revenue likely to inflect sharply in coming
quarters. OCS, multi-rail, and CPO/NPO opportunities could follow later in the
fiscal year and contribute more materially in FY28. We also expect gross
margin to trough in F1Q27 before improving sequentially each quarter,
supported by product ramps, moderating FX headwinds, and potentially a more
favorable mix from next-generation opportunities in the back half. Together,
these drivers should support a beat-and-raise and build investor confidence in
the FY27 growth acceleration. The reaction could be muted, however, if the new
segment reporting limits visibility into the specific programs investors have
focused on in recent quarters. To that end, we are modestly adjusting our
forecasts while leaving our out-year outlook largely unchanged and lower our
Dec-27 price target to $465 (vs. $695 prior), based on a lower 17x target
multiple or below the multiples we ascribe to Coherent and Lumentum, but above
those for EMS peers, reflecting Fabrinet’s niche optical exposure and higher
gross margins.

  * F1Q27 (Sep-end) Results: Expect revenue, operating margins and earnings to track ahead of consensus expectations. We are forecasting revenue of $1,426 mn vs. consensus $1,407 mn and guidance of $1,375-$1,425 mn, representing growth of +46% y/y. Meanwhile, we are forecasting gross margins of 12.1% (vs. consensus of 12.2%) and operating margins of 11.0% (vs. consensus of 10.9%), which leads to our earnings forecast of $4.27 (vs. consensus of $4.19 and guidance of $4.10-$4.25).
  * F2Q27 (Dec-end) Guidance: Revenue and earnings outlook anticipated to track ahead of sell-side estimates. We are forecasting revenue of $1,536 mn vs. consensus $1,478 mn, representing growth of +36% y/y. Meanwhile, we are forecasting gross margins of 12.2% (vs. consensus of 12.3%) and operating margins of 11.0% (vs. consensus of 11.1%), which leads to our earnings forecast of $4.56 (vs. consensus of $4.43).



#

### Lumentum (Overweight; Price Target: $1,280.00)

### Investment Thesis

Increased exposure to the Datacom segment, which is facing AI-led growth in
demand, via the recent acquisition of Cloud Light, positions LITE shares as a
potential pick to play the AI theme. Additionally, with the headwinds
including share loss in 3D Sensing as well as inventory rationalization from
Telecom and Datacom customers well baked into estimates, and the shares
trading inexpensive based on our CY28 estimates, which is essentially below
the long-term historical multiple, we rate LITE shares Overweight.

### Valuation

Our December 2027 price target of $1,280 is based on valuing our CY28E EPS
estimate at a ~29x P/E target multiple. The multiple is ahead of the average
historical multiple at which the company has traded, and we believe it is
justified given benefits from demand relative to AI investments.

**_AAPL: F4Q Recap – Pricing Power Drives Hardware Upside, but Services

 _Inmy Off The Call
note
last night, I shared view that Apple's September quarter was solid – with
memory worries well understood (the step-down in the GM guide was still
painful, but it’s a crowded short), and iPhone holding up well. The surprise
was the deceleration in Services growth (to only a gui de of +8~9% YoY),
driven by weaker third-party licensing/gaming and FX. Increased OpEx (as
agentic Siri grows) and limited visibility on component costs remain
overhangs, though nothing here is thesis-changing. The ~35x earnings multiple
(top of range), however, prices the stock for perfection, and we didn’t get
that this print. _

Samik Chatterjee weighs in on the solid quarter, but warns that F1Q27 guidance
shows the tension investors need to watch: **the revenue growth guide of
+7-10%YoY is well above Street** (JPMe +3%, consensus +6%), **yet gross margin
guide of 45-46% is below Street's 46.7%** as memory cost headwinds (DRAM/NAND
pricing "unprecedented," per management) bite harder than expected and persist
beyond the Dec-Q, now also constraining Mac/iPad supply alongside iPhone Duo.
**Services growth is also decelerating further** , guided to +8-9%YoY (v. JPMe
+13%, consensus +12%) on 3P licensing and FX headwinds, raising longer-term
questions on the Services growth algorithm. Indeed, Samik frames it as a
“changing trajectory of Hardware vs. Services growth”: _“despite the concerns
around supply constraints as well as price elasticity following significant
price increases, Product (and iPhone) revenues have delivered to expectations,
while on the flip-side we have seen a steady moderation in the growth rate for
Services, which is increasingly going to call into question the long-term
Services growth rate when faced with mobile gaming headwinds, app store
business model changes and 3P licensing (i.e. including Google in our view)
headwinds.”_ Samik takes down is EPS, and with it his TP by a hair.





**_CALX: Margin Strength Offsets Softer Revenue, but 4Q Margin Trajectory
Raises Flags._**

CALX printed amc yesterday and hosts its call at 8:30am today, and the stock
traded a few points lower. Joseph Cardoso commented that **3Q26 revenue landed
modestly below JPMe & consensus on softer Appliance and Software & Service
trends, but gross margin hit the high end of guidance** as memory surcharges
offset higher component costs, while Software & Service gross margin hit a
record 67%+, driving an opex-in-line operating margin and earnings beat.
**Capital return remains robust**. **Guidance, though, is only in line with
consensus** , implying flat GMs and lower OPM sequentially, a departure from
management's earlier call for a 3Q GM trough. _Key watchpoints for Joe on the
call today are commentary on timing of growth acceleration from agentic
workflows/Calix One, the margin recovery path amid rising component costs, and
FCF trajectory as it compresses._

Story._**

its 14th straight quarter of growth** and 7th straight of accelerating YoY
growth, with strength broad-based across Data Center (TRx/DCI/HPC), Comms
Infra, and Auto/Industrial. Margins were a modest soft spot. **F2Q27 guidance
came in well above expectations** , and _management flagged the AWS TRx
program moving from qualification to adoption_ , alongside OCS and NPO each
framed as potential multi-hundred-million-dollar opportunities. _The real
catalyst is the capacity story_ : revenue capacity is set to roughly double

upgrade, citing **choppier near-term customer ramp visibility** and limited
clarity on new customer ramps as capping near-term upside despite a
constructive long-term AI/optical thesis.
